yaml.description: Classical machine learning worked through one algorithm at a time: what it assumes, where it breaks, and a runnable example for each.
yaml.title: ML Methods

markdown.markdown:
<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This is the pre-deep-learning half of machine learning, the part that still solves most problems that arrive as a table of numbers. Each page takes one algorithm, states the intuition in a line, lists what it is good and bad at, then works an example in scikit-learn.

Several algorithms get two pages: one for the method and one marked `TUT` applying it to a real dataset. Read them as a pair.

For neural networks see [DL Methods](https://bthek1.github.io/DL_methods/), and for forecasting see [Time Series](https://bthek1.github.io/TimeSeriesML/).

---


The parts that apply no matter which model you pick.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Training and Testing](00_train_test_split.ipynb) | Why you hold data back at all, and how `train_test_split` does it |
| [Loss and Cost Functions](07_Loss_or_Cost_funtions.ipynb) | The common losses, and which ones suit classification against regression |
| [L1 and L2 Regularization](06_L1_and_L2%20Regularization.ipynb) | Overfitting shown on a plain regression, then Lasso and Ridge as the fix |
| [Hyper-parameter Optimization](08_HyperParameterOptimization.ipynb) | Three escalating approaches: manual trial and error over a split, then K-fold cross validation, then `GridSearchCV` |

---

## Regression

Predicting a continuous value.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Linear Regression](030_LinearRegression.ipynb) | The single-variable case, ending in generated house price predictions |
| [Multi-Linear Regression](031_Multi-LinearRegression.ipynb) | The same with several input variables |
| [Polynomial Regression](05_PolynomialRegression.ipynb) | Fitting curves, second order and higher |
| [Kernel Ridge Regression](15_KernalsRidgeRegression.ipynb) | Ridge regression combined with the kernel trick, for non-linear relationships |
| [Support Vector Regression](11_SVM.ipynb) | SVM applied to a continuous target |

---

## Classification

Predicting a category.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [K-NN](01_K-NN.ipynb) | Take any point, it is what it is close to. Distance metrics, choosing k, then a first model and a `GridSearchCV` search for the optimum |
| [Decision Tree](02_DecisionTree.ipynb) | If-statements placed where entropy drops fastest, plus the trade-offs of CART |
| [Logistic Regression](04_LogisticRegression.ipynb) | Binary and multiclass, and the classification types each suits |
| [Naive Bayes](100_Bayesian.ipynb) | The Bayesian approach and Gaussian processes |
| [Naive Bayes Tutorial](101_Naive_Bayes_TUT.ipynb) | The same method built into an email spam filter |
| [Random Forest](12_Random_forest.ipynb) | Many trees voting |

---

## Ensembles

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Ensemble Methods](090_Ensemble.ipynb) | Bagging against boosting, and when each helps |
| [Ensemble Tutorial](091_Ensemble_TUT.ipynb) | Bagging applied to heart disease prediction, then boosting |
| [Bagging: Diabetes Prediction](092_bagging_diabetes_prediction.ipynb) | A second worked bagging example |

---

## Unsupervised Learning

Finding structure without labels.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Principal Component Analysis](130_PCA.ipynb) | Dimensionality reduction |
| [PCA Tutorial](131_PCA_TUT.ipynb) | PCA applied to heart disease prediction |
| [Gaussian Mixture Models](19_Gaussian_mixture_models.ipynb) | Modelling data as a mixture of Gaussians, the expectation-maximization algorithm behind it, and its use for clustering, density estimation, and anomaly detection |
| [K-Means Clustering](20_K_mean_clustering.ipynb) | The algorithm step by step, choosing K, and the alternatives when it does not fit |

---

## GPU Programming

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [CUDA](18_CUDA.ipynb) | The odd one out, and the longest page here. Getting a CUDA toolchain working, then writing kernels: RGB to greyscale, then matrix multiplication. Useful background for why the deep learning libraries are shaped the way they are |

---

## Not Covered Yet

- **Three pages are placeholders** marked "coming soon" with no content: [CNNs](14_CNNs.ipynb), [Generative Models](16_Generative.ipynb), and [Back Propagation](17_BackPropagation.ipynb). All three are really deep learning topics and are covered properly in [DL Methods](https://bthek1.github.io/DL_methods/).
- **Nothing on gradient boosting libraries.** No XGBoost, LightGBM, or CatBoost page, despite them being the usual winners on tabular data. XGBoost is covered from the forecasting angle in [Time Series](https://bthek1.github.io/TimeSeriesML/).
- **No feature engineering page**, and no treatment of missing data, categorical encoding, or scaling as topics in their own right.
- **No model interpretability**: nothing on SHAP, permutation importance, or partial dependence.
- Evaluation is spread through the tutorials rather than collected anywhere, so there is no single page on precision, recall, ROC, or calibration.

---
